newsitem.title: UK: UK shares hold solid gains in record territory.
newsitem.headline: UK shares hold solid gains in record territory.

text.p: UK's FTSE 100 index was holding solid gains at midday on Tuesday, well into record territory, and dealers said the market looked set to move higher still with a firmer start on Wall Street.
By 1300 GMT, the leading blue chip index was up 33.4 points to 4,703.0, off an all-time high set earlier at 4,720.3.
Dealers' books, said one dealer, "are too short and there's this panic that they'll be caught if the Street does better this afternoon."
The Dow was expected to resume its advance after news that U.S. retail sales fell 0.3 percent in April, as expected.

The market is still awaiting U.S. producer and consumer inflation data, due later this week, for a stronger indication of whether the Federal Reserve will move to tighten credit further when its policy-making committee meets on May 20, dealers said.
"The figures were smack in line and that's being viewed as a bullish sign," the dealer said. "They would have had to have been pretty bad for the market to come off significantly."
And with U.S. blue chips once again soaring over 100 points overnight against a background of falling bond yields, any correction would be slight and shortlived, another dealer said.
"There is still a lot of money pouring into the U.S. market. People aren't expecting any aggressive Fed rate hikes so bond yields are dropping," another dealer said.

The FTSE 100 hit its best ever levels earlier, even as the Bank of England's first quarter inflation indicated that further "moderate" policy tightening was needed in order to prevent inflation spiking above the British government's target rate of 2.5 percent.
Yet dealers said key for the UK share market as well as the Dow would be U.S. interest rate policy.
Last Thursday, Fed chairman Alan Greenspan cast some doubt on the need for any near-term increase in U.S. rates following a 1/4 point hike in March.
Among UK blue chips, shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc, SmithKline Beecham Plc and Zeneca Group Plc leapt to record peaks as renewed investment demand caught the market short of stock, dealers said.
Glaxo shares were up 39-1/2p to 1251, while SmithKline surged 53p to 1095. Zeneca jumped 27p to 1970.
Shares in Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc dropped, paring Monday's sharp gains as euphoria faded on their surprise merger agreement, dealers said.
Guinness, rated a "sell" by Dresdner Kleinwort Benson on Tuesday, was down 12-1/2p at 590, while Grand Met fell 10-1/2p to 581.

SocGen also lowered its ratings on Guinness and Grand Met, to "hold" from "buy," arguing that the benefits of the merger -- particularly their presence in emerging markets -- were hard to quantify and could take a long time to show through.
Elsewhere in the sector, shares in Allied Domecq Plc jumped 18-1/2p to 465 after reporting first half pre-tax profits of 317 million stg, in-line with market expectations.
The stock rose on Monday as the planned merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan Plc sparked bid speculation across the industry.
BOC Plc gained 9p to 984-1/2 after reporting six-month pre-tax profits of 216.4 million stg versus 217.4 million a year ago, at the top end of analysts' forecasts.
